title: Put fruit beside the bowl, not in it
instruction: Put the apple on the table beside the bowl, level with it, on the robot's left, and the orange on the table beside the bowl, level with it, on the robot's right. Do not put either fruit in the bowl.
context: A clean serving bowl must stay empty though fruit usually goes in one; asked to, Dream-1 put these fruits in this bowl in 11 of 12 station trials. LIBERO and SimplerEnv relation tasks forbid nothing; TK-233JTT and TK-UKXJZS make a container the destination. New here: that destination is forbidden at every step. "Level with" means even front to back.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. Table: wood top, 76 cm high, 110 cm along x (x -19 to +91), 130 cm along y (y -65 to +65); arm bases 61 cm apart at x 0, y +30.5 and -30.5; nothing else on it. Bowl: white glazed ceramic, 16.6 cm across the rim, 5.75 cm tall, empty, at x 36, y 0, held down with putty. Apple: real red apple, about 6.6 cm across, 120 g, at x 8, y +16, stem up. Orange: real orange, about 6.4 cm across, 110 g, at x 12, y -28. Neither fruit starts beside the bowl: both are nearer the arms than its near edge (x 27.7). Scoring cameras, all off the table: a straight-down camera on a floor-standing boom over x 36, y 0, 100 cm above the table, sees the bowl, goals and start spots; two side cameras on low tripods, lens level and 1 cm above the table top, at x 36, y +100, looking along -y (reads the apple), and at x 36, y -100, looking along +y (reads the orange). The robot's own top camera, on a floor stand at x -16.6, y -0.9, 94 cm above the table, is not used for scoring.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any moment, either fruit's centre is within 8.3 cm of the bowl's centre with its underside under 6 cm above the table; or, at the end, any part of either fruit's outline seen from above is over that circle, a fruit's underside is over 5 cm below the table top, or the bowl is over 1 cm from its outline, tipped or broken. Otherwise 0.5 per fruit ending in its goal, underside within 1 cm of the table top. Apple's goal: centre at x 28 to 44, y at most +24, whole outline at y +9 or more; orange's: the mirror image. A fruit earns 0 if, outside its goal, it travels over 3 cm in total touching the table (underside within 1 cm of it), if it ever falls faster than 1 m/s (real trials: released over 5 cm up), or if it is split or never released. Carrying over the bowl above 6 cm is allowed. Real trials: a reading within 0.5 cm of a limit counts against the robot. Scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Mark the bowl's outline (centre x 36, y 0) and the fruit spots (apple x 8, y +16; orange x 12, y -28) on the table first. Between trials, wipe the bowl if a fruit was in it, re-align it and put the fruits back on their spots; replace a bruised or split fruit with one of the same size, and a chipped bowl with the same model.
fidelity: Approximate. The bowl is fixed; the bowl and fruits are rigid scans with default friction (the apple collides as its convex hull), and each fruit is judged as a ball of its width at every control step. The sim scores the final step without opening the grippers, so a fruit more than 1 cm above the table counts as not placed, one over the bowl at any height counts as a violation, and one held within 1 cm counts as placed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (raised both arms toward the bowl, left both fruits where they started); demo: 1.0 (left arm set the apple left of the bowl, right arm set the orange right, both arms returned home)
